body.statement: For a sequence with \(T\) and cycle rank \(q\) increasing, characterize the weakest graph-spectrum and moment conditions under which a feasible regularized cycle correction is asymptotically linear for \(\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}\), attains the relevant growing-dimensional efficiency frontier, and supports valid studentization, using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{grow}}\) as the construction handle.
body.justification: The fixed-horizon theorem leaves open how many noisy overidentifying cycle directions can be exploited when adoption calendars lengthen.
body.gap: Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024, Theorems 1--2) treat additive efficient imputation at fixed design dimension and do not analyze a growing weighted cycle Gram spectrum for a proportional ratio.
body.consumer: A solution would provide principled regularization and inference for long staggered panels with many pretreatment cycles.

obligation.what_is_open: A growing-dimensional theorem requires a specified triangular-array model for \(T_N\), \(q_N\), cohort shares, graph spectra, tail envelopes, and a concrete spectral regularization rule; the frozen handle does not define these objects or an ordering under which one set of conditions could be called weakest.
obligation.obstruction: Pointwise finite fourth moments at each fixed law do not control the smallest nonzero eigenvalues of \(K_N\), the operator error of \(\widehat K_N\), the high-dimensional cycle-score approximation, or studentization uniformly as \(q_N\) grows. Assuming those conclusions would assume the crux, while the fixed-horizon core supplies no triangular-array class from which to derive them.
obligation.attempted: The fixed-dimensional spectral projection was decomposed into retained-cycle stochastic error and discarded-loading bias. Closing either term for increasing \(q_N\) needs, respectively, a uniform self-normalized central limit condition and quantitative eigenvalue/loading decay assumptions not present in the frozen core.
obligation.partial_result:
For every fixed \(T\) and fixed \(q\), the proved expansion is
\[
\sqrt N(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}})
=
\{h_{\mathrm{CM}}-R(R^{\prime}\Omega R)^{-1}
R^{\prime}\Omega h_{\mathrm{CM}}\}^{\prime}
\sqrt N(\overline Y-m)+o_P(1),
\]
with consistent studentization. This establishes the complete fixed-dimensional boundary case but does not determine a growing-\(q\) regularization frontier.
